aj: Hey team — spotted a weird skew in canary exposure when per-tier routing + quota filters run. We configured 10% global canary, with per-tier scope: gold=50%, silver=30%, bronze=20%. But after quota/entitlement filtering the effective exposure for gold is ~3% instead of the intended ~5%. Is the canonical semantics: (A) compute per-scope target and enforce (clamp) after filtering, or (B) compute global target then rescale to available capacity after filtering?

jun: Current impl is (B) — we take the global 10% then rescale across scopes after applying entitlement/tenant-eligibility checks. That makes sense for preserving global budget but does violate per-tier intent.

maria: I'd vote for (A) as the default for canaries. If product scoped the rollout to give gold more exposure, we should treat scope targets as first-class. Fallbacks should be separate: if a scope can't hit target, notify and optionally backfill from global pool but don't silently steal from other scopes.

kevin: that sounds right functionally but complexity spikes. With strict per-scope targets we may exceed capacity or surge quotas if multiple scopes become eligible simultaneously. We need an explicit API knob: e.g. `exposure_mode: "per_scope_strict" | "global_rescale"`. Also a max-capacity check so we don't overcommit.

aj: Agreed on an API flag. Drafting a minimal policy shape — thoughts?
```
{
  "policy_name": "canary-v2",
  "global_target_pct": 10,
  "scopes": {
    "gold": 50,
    "silver": 30,
    "bronze": 20
  },
  "exposure_mode": "per_scope_strict", // or "global_rescale"
  "fallback": {
    "allow_backfill": false,
    "backfill_sources": ["global_pool"],
    "priority": ["gold","silver","bronze"]
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: route_policy_v2 staged to canary pool in us-west-2 — deploy id: dp-1901-cc. Link: https://deploys.internal/release/dp-1901-cc :rocket:

opt-bot: telemetry recs: tag every decision with `routing_policy_version`, `exposure_mode`, `scope_requested`, `scope_effective_pct`, `fallback_reason` (e.g., quota, region_unavailable), and `quota_applied`. Emit histogram `effective_exposure_per_scope` and a counter `fallback_triggered` with labels (scope, reason). Traces should include the evaluated policy snippet.

maria: For Console UX we need two small tiles on the rollout detail page: 1) per-tier intended vs actual exposure (time-series), 2) fallback events stream (with tenant id, reason, and suggested action). Also an alert rule when any scope underdelivers by >25% for 10m.

jun: Plan: 1) add `exposure_mode` flag to routing API + server-side enforcement paths (2) wire the telemetry labels that opt-bot suggested (3) add short-term Console metric tiles as a first pass. I'll open a PR with tests for both modes.

kevin: +1. assign me to perf/limits review. I'll add capacity guards and a sim harness to check worst-case backfill behaviour.

aj: thanks — message captured. @maria please sketch the console mockups and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
